snippet.textDisplay: Trang trí lắp kẻ ngoài cho nó trông đẹp giống như kiểu là búp bê bjd đi nhìn đẹp hơn, hoặc nhìn giống búp bê người đẹp hơn Ai ác ý không thích thì thôi chứ nhìn vẻ ngoài giống búp bê khớp BJD người đẹp có thể thay tóc,quần áo ,mắt lắp cho nó bằng loại áp tròng kính mắt nhìn được vi khuẩn các tia cực tím mà mắt người không nhìn được,giọng nói hay,tôi ưu nó như người trợ lý bảo vệ khỏi kẻ tấn công hơn là những con người ác ý gọi là thây ma hay kẻ hủy diệt, lấy việc họ không thích họ áp đặt cho người khác, tôi ưu hình dạng búp bê khớp cầu hay 3d người đẹp trai,gái hơn người mắt là các thấu kính để nhìn và cảnh báo,độ dẻo để phục vụ chăm sóc việc nhà và công việc,có giọng nói lắp chip Al để nhớ và hiểu lênh có bộ xoá và bộ chống hack cơ công nghệ cao, Chứ bây giờ một con robot đương nhiên hơn những con người ác ý mất dạy bình luận, Nó giúp thật và không ác ý như con người, còn những con người ác ý quá mệt mỏi với họ lúc nào cũng gây áp lực rất hận thù hận vì quan hệ tình dục hay cái gì mất dạy hay là nói những cái câu nói mất dạy gây uất hận thù hận chán ghét phong tục chửi bậy của con người và đương nhiên một con robot không tấn công con người vẫn tốt hơn loài người nhiều, đỡ mệt người và đau não

snippet.textDisplay:
Ok. Robots are now moving more efficiently than humans. It's going to be simultaneously depressing and awe inspiring to watch them do our manual labor jobs better than us. This is a decade away but right now cognitive based jobs are already being replaced by AI. 
The bright side, if there is one, is that once the price of goods and services plumet to ridiculous lows, governments will be able to put everyone on Universal Basic Income and most people will be making more money by not working. A lot of people fear this, because they think that their jobs give them purpose and meaning in life, but once you have time to explore all the avenues that you were never able to, because you were too busy being a slave, you will find new purpose and meaning. Imagine being able to watch your children grow up, instead of being at work 1/3 of your life. Or being able to work on personal projects like creating music, art, crafts. Philosophy. Self discovery. Being more present in your own life instead of spending your days helping someone else get ritch. You could even have more time to get ritch yourself while have UBI to fall back on. It's not as dark as everyone tries to paint it. 

And I'm not a bot by-the-way 😂
I'm a real person damn it! 😂

I know, I know, "That’s exactly what a bot would say"

But think about. Free money, and all of your time back. Time is the only resource in life that you can't get back. Once it's gone, it's gone.

snippet.textDisplay:
That right there is why Boston Dynamics is still the standard robots are measured by. Plenty of companies can stage a cool demo. Very few can demonstrate full body dynamic control, industrial robustness, and a clear path to deployment.

Atlas isn’t impressive because it can move like a gymnast, do back flips and kung fu. It’s impressive because it moves dynamically. It doesn’t just follow pre scripted motions. It calculates balance, force, and momentum in real time. It recovers from disturbances. It coordinates its entire body as one system. That is a control problem most humanoids still struggle with.
Then there is the hardware. High power electric actuators. Dozens of degrees of freedom. The strength to manipulate real industrial loads. This is not a fragile lab prototype posing for cameras. It is being designed for factory floors and real workflows.

That is the difference. 😉

​​@Deliveredmean42You make some fair points and you're coping well.

Tell me more about the brisk pace at which US robotics companies are moving to overcome the obstacles you mention.

How many times have Boston Dynamics done anything as "simple" as Unitree just showed they can?

Is the USA far ahead in battery technology? You would think we might know, if they were.

I think the difference is, atlas is a industry bot that can sometimes pull of gymnastics while the Chinese bots are gymnastic bots that have no industry uses. The Chinese bots have been slimmed down for savings on weight and more agility, we have no idea if they can do the -4f(~-20c)-104f(~40c) temperature range and 110lbs(~50kg) lift capacity of atlas.

Also as shown atlas focuses on many degrees of freedom as possible, which leads to more failure points, the fact that the flips we have seen it fail led to only small damage is incredible.

Im not saying the Chinese bots are not impressive, Boston dynamics took a long time to get humanoids which they have posted publically and their movements are very natural.

Personally, I don't believe that the robot threat is that imminent. I've seen videos of the real top of the crop robots, and currently they are not capable of walking on two legs. They can look humanoid while standing still or sitting, but all the footage of them doing jumping jacks and walking around in a warehouse as featured in this video... they are far removed from that.

Apparently programming in balance is incredibly difficult. And I hope they keep insisting on this human look rather than more field-specific practical designs because the human look is going to take them _so so much longer_.

I'm not saying I agree with how these corporations are using AI. But one of the things we don't do as Americans is look at our history, study it, and see how it's repeating.

Two very big things are happening right now that have already occurred in history. One, we see a group of people supporting a fascist dictator. He makes promises to the people that things are going to be better, while making decisions for a self-serving agenda. Tr*mp/Hitler.

The second thing going on right now is an industrial revolution again. At the turn of the century an industrial revolution took place that did put a lot of people out of work.

History is repeating itself here. This change created industries where people had to become more specialized. People were used to provincial farming had to learn new skills. This is no different. If you want to survive the changes you have to adapt the same way people back around the turn of the century had to.

Change is hard, but also inevitable. And we are going to be doomed to repeat the same mistakes in history if we don't learn from them.

It’s a double edge sword. Ai, Robotics, you’d have to agree that all this is amazing but when you look at the rapidity here it becomes very concerning when you realise the level of destabilisation that we will start  experience, if not already. For example:

1. Robots take over the worker’s roles/jobs
2. The argument, new jobs , less tedious, not as risky, hazardous or dangerous will be created. 
3. Workers can be retrained as these changes in advancements are rolled out.
4. Workers need to be retrained and implemented in time, before the intelligent robots advance and absorb these new roles / jobs /duties etc only just created, originally for us humans?
5. How many shareholders are going to accept the fact these companies they’ve invested in aren’t making more money because they haven’t put in place more Ai and Robotics thus reducing the employment of costly humans?
6. And who are the manufacturers that the companies are making products for and the retail sectors are selling them to and the services provided to?

let’s face it, we have many questions that need to be asked, will we be able to afford living in this age if a majority of us are jobless? Will society evolve as it collapses??? It’s been a freight train approach and we all have a responsibility to be smart about this because if you don’t see it already, we’ve already been partially blindsided.

That's the third revolution coming. First we had the industrial revolution, where machines and factories increased productivity of workers. 

Then we had the agricultural revolution, where mechanized agriculture led to us only needing less than 10% of the population to grow crops instead of the former 90%.

And the third revolution will be robots replacing line workers in factories, pickers in warehouses and similar jobs. 

And just like with the previous two it will be really hard on those getting replaced and take decades to settle into a new sustainable normal. 

The real issue will be that AI threatens service and knowledge workers at the same time, making it really hard to imagine an out for all those replaced by robots.

snippet.textDisplay:
I understand the concerns about automation replacing workers in factories—especially for families where generations have relied on these jobs for survival and dignity. These roles aren’t just economic; they’re personal, generational, and often the only path many have had to stability.

Big corporations often see only numbers on a balance sheet, not the faces and futures behind those numbers. They calculate efficiency gains but don’t calculate the emotional toll of uncertainty on communities. And if our government already fails to adequately support those dependent on its systems, how can we expect it to safeguard the workers who will be displaced by automation? Businesses certainly won't—once labor is replaced, those people are no longer "assets" to them.

What’s even more frustrating is this: instead of investing time, money, and serious thought into education and preparing Americans for the jobs of the future, we’re still pushing people toward physically punishing, low-paying work. I’ve done those jobs. They are not easy, and they’re not sustainable unless you’re young or conditioned by years of it. Middle-aged workers—especially newcomers—will struggle. And once they’re broken by the work, then what?

If someone chooses to work those jobs, that’s fine—more power to them. But let’s not pretend this is about opportunity. This is about systemic neglect. We need to build a future where people can choose their path—not be cornered into it because there’s nothing else.

snippet.textDisplay:
Robots and AI are unavoidable.

What is avoidable is a social and humanitarian crisis of unseen proportions due to human employees being laid off and having nowhere to go. To avoid this, the entire world needs to come together and agree on social stimuli and welfare terms.

The US is currently distancing itself from every ally it ever had, and breaking every single international agreement on ethical regulations or humanitarian support. So what's likely to happen is for some labour-abusive countries (China, Russia, and other smaller economies) to fully automate without caring about humans at all, and produce cheap consumer goods, leaving the US out of it, since all they do is impose tariffs while refusing to be a team player. With this isolationist stance, the US will leave its former allies to fend for themselves and they'll likely buy from China, so even if their (ex-allies) idea of AI automation was ethical, it doesn't matter since they won't compete with the cost to produce goods, and their impoverished populations will demand to access those cheap goods. They could form a coalition and also tariff China to smithereens, reducing their market reach. Maybe this is the beginning of the end of the big empires, if the coalition can hold their line and remain ethical and human-centered. Would still come at the cost of blood, sweat and tears.

Basically we're fucked, unless the world leaders come together and figure this out as a collective and as allies against the unethical rollout of AI Automation.

I… do not think this is happening.  Will people be replaced by robots?  Yes this is happening, but it won’t be by these.  They’re too expensive, too prone to errors and breaking.  They just won’t be robust enough for this sort of work and environment any time soon if ever.  But. So look at how long that would be financially feasible where you are now, and that’ll be roughly how long you have for your job if that’s relevant to you.  For say automotive manufacturing assembly lines are typically built to last around 10 years until they restructure it.  It won’t be immediately, but it won’t be long either.

And for reference I do not think this is good for the people or economy.  But I’m in the industry and have some idea about how this is going currently.  The humanoid robots aren’t typically going well.  But other types of technology are.

U.S. pressure accelerated the deal. But India and the EU were already negotiating this for almost 20 years. Trump didn’t invent the impulse. He removed the procrastination.
Does this pull trade away from the U.S.?
Some trade diversion will happen, but it’s selective and incremental.
Here’s how trade actually shifts in reality, not headlines:
• European cars, wine, machinery, and chemicals become cheaper in India
• Indian textiles, leather goods, and engineering products become cheaper in Europe
• In those categories, U.S. exporters lose some price competitiveness
That means:
A German car may beat an American car in India
An Indian textile shipment may go to Europe instead of the U.S.
That’s trade reallocation, not trade collapse.
Will U.S. GDP be negatively impacted?
Yes, but mildly. Think ripples, not waves.

• In those categories, U.S. exporters lose some price competitiveness
That means:
A German car may beat an American car in India
An Indian textile shipment may go to Europe instead of the U.S.
That’s trade reallocation, not trade collapse.
Will U.S. GDP be negatively impacted?
Yes, but mildly. Think ripples, not waves.

Unitree Robotics (Left Robot)
The Unitree G1 was created by Unitree Robotics (Hangzhou Yushu Technology Co., Ltd.), a leading robotics company based in Hangzhou, China. 
Founder: The company was founded in 2016 by Wang Xingxing, who previously developed the XDog quadruped as a student.
Focus: Unitree is known for making high-performance robots more accessible and affordable, with the G1 starting at approximately $16,000. 
Boston Dynamics (Right Robot)
The all-electric Atlas was developed by Boston Dynamics, an American robotics firm headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts. 
Parent Company: Since 2021, Boston Dynamics has been owned by the Hyundai Motor Group.
History: Founded in 1992 as a spin-off from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) by Marc Raibert, the company has spent decades developing advanced bipedal and quadrupedal robots.

From Chatgpt query entering your claim:
The Current Reality: "Made in China" for Robots
The statement you heard might have been true 10 or even 5 years ago. Now, it's the opposite. The Rise of Domestic Champions: Companies like Estun Automation, Inovance, Siasun, and Efort have grown into massive players. They produce a huge range of robots, from the large robotic arms used in car manufacturing to the smaller, precise "SCARA" robots used for assembling phones.

The Electric Vehicle (EV) Boom: This is the biggest factor. China's EV industry, led by companies like BYD, Zeekr, and Nio, has exploded. These companies needed massive amounts of automation to build cars quickly and efficiently. Chinese robot companies were right there, ready to supply them. They understood the local needs, could provide faster service, and were often cheaper.

Vertical Integration (like Xiaomi): Some of the biggest manufacturers have started building their own automation solutions. Xiaomi, for example, has its own very advanced fully automated "lighthouse" factory for producing its flagship phones. While they might use some standard robots from partners, much of the integration and custom automation is developed in-house. It's not a foreign company coming in to set it up; it's Xiaomi's own engineers.

■ 코스피 5000의 속빈강정

삼전 하이닉스와

바이오 로봇은 적자 자본잠식 종목을 전환사채 증자헐값에 받은 증끈사와 사채업자가 증끈사리포트 주가전망 찌라시 뉴스로 뻥튀기 사기증시를 46년간 사기증시로 몰고왔다

거기에는 불공정 악법이 원인제공을 해왔다

세금기준이 주가기준의 몰상식 비상식 악법이 코리아디스카운터의 원인제공

주가와 지수상승의 걸림돌이었다

세금 적게내려고 지주사종목의 주가 누르기

그래서 세금기준을 순자산기준으로 변겨오개정을 필자는 3년전부터 윤통이 증권거래소 재방문하도록까지한 사람이다

일본처럼 PBR 1배이하 퇴출시키도록하면 닛케이싀소사상최고가로 달리는걸 롤모델로 삼아야된다고 또 상속세가 65%로 과도하여 적게내려고 주가를 누른다고

결국 새정부가 상법개정에 반영되었다

자산가치와 수익성을 기준으로 변경 개정시킨싀 3달이 지났다


매도1순위다 레인보우 뉴로메카 로보티즈 클로봇 휴림로봇 유지로봇 등 전 로봇종목들과 바이오는 매도하고 종목삭제하라
현대차 외에는 살아날 종목 없다

바이오 로봇이 양극화 사기증시의 주범이다

■●지주사 세방 삼양홀딩스 등등 지주사 종목으로 갈아타야 안전하게 400%묵을수있다



https://naver.me/5ixHdGIO



세방은

자회사 세방전지 자회사와 39개 계열사를 거느린 세방그룹이다

세방전지는 현대차 기아에 세방 로케트밧데리와 전기차 리튬밧데리 모듈을 장착하고있다

당기순이익 1700억인데 세방이 지분 40%라 1700×0.4=680억이 세방으로 들어온다

이번에 배당을 25%로 올렸다

세방의 유보율 1조109억

세방전지 유보율 2조 3000억

세방 PBR 0.25배로

주당순자산 BPS 54300원인데

현재가14000원도 안되는 청산가치의 1/4 주가임을 알수있다

​​​@minhkim9438에궁~
여긴 그냥 일반인들이  자기 머릿속 생각만으로 모든게맞다고 확신하는 듯합니다.
그러면서 아는척 한마디씩 다 던지죠.

내가 이런분야 국책기관에서 연구하는 사람인데도  전부  자기주장 한마디씩 하네요

(힌트) 지대공 미사일(능동추적 가정)이 비행기를 추적하는데 비행기가 방향을 바꾸면 어덯게 되나요?  바꾸어 계속 추적하쟌아요.  그런 함수가  있어요.  정확히는 비선형 미븐방정식인데 (- 무한대에서 최근까지 업데이트(이를 이노베아션 이라함)로 하면서 무한히 계속 추적합니다.
단, 임계치가 넘어가면 놓칠 수는 있어요.

로봇의 제어도 똑같습니다.  일정 범위내에 있으면 균형점이 틀어지면 다시 제어점을 찾아 균형을 맞춥니다.
물론 이것도 임계치 범위내에 있어야 합니다. 사실 제어에서 가장 중요한것 하나가 stability 인데 이 안정도 범위내에 있도록 제어데상을 설계합니다.

보통 사람들이 생각하는 것처럼 쉬우면  모두 다 하지요. 자동으로 스스로 찾아가는 시스템 정도는 돼야 연구진이 개입해서 설계하지요. 

제어공학은 80%가 수학입니다.  대부분 복소확률 미부낭정식 입니다.  디지털제어에서는 복소확률차분방정식이 되겠네요. 이 미분 방정식의 해가 일반저으로 그ㅏ기 어려워서 자기반복적 근사해를 구하는 보잡한 수치해석적 방벙을  사용합니다.  수식만 2페이지나 됩니다.

복소수, 확률, 무한급수, 미분적븐, 방정식 , 행렬, 여기에 시간함수 및  수치해석 등 왠만한 수학 다 동원됩니다
  
고드학교때 수학 배워서 어디에 서요? 이런 질문 많이 하는데 고등학교 수학은 수학이라고 하지 않을 정도입니다. 대학에서 고차원 수학 배우는데 이것도 상식 범위에요. 석박사과정에서 다시 더 고차원 수학 배우는데 이정도는 돼야 적용가능합니다.

​@reubenbirch .. Redundancy in robotics describes a system that has more joints than minimally necessary to perform a task. Atlas, when fully outfitted, has i think 56 DOF. If you discount the hands and fingers, atlas probably has well over 20 DOF being utilized for this stunt. That's an enormous (effectively infinite) number of joint position solution combinations to arrive at the same result. Parsing which combination in real time strikes me as perfectly suited to Ai.

Human shaped robots are basically just a vanity project for humans to create a subservient species similar to us. Real militarized robots will come in the form of armoured drones and AI guided missiles, I seriously doubt we’ll ever see a bunch of human shaped robots marching into battle, that would be a waste of materials and money when a dozen drones could do the same job without ever having to face the dreaded flip floppy stair problem that these tin cans seem to struggle with.

snippet.textDisplay:
An electromagnetic pulse (EMP), also referred to as a transient electromagnetic disturbance (TED), is a brief burst of electromagnetic energy. The origin of an EMP can be natural or artificial, and can occur as an electromagnetic field, as an electric field, as a magnetic field, or as a conducted electric current. The electromagnetic interference caused by an EMP can disrupt communications and damage electronic equipment.[1] An EMP such as a lightning strike can physically damage objects such as buildings and aircraft. The management of EMP effects is a branch of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) engineering.

The first recorded damage from an electromagnetic pulse came with the solar storm of August 1859, or the Carrington Event.[2]

For modern warfare, weapons delivering a high energy EMP are designed to disrupt[3] communications equipment, computers needed to operate modern warplanes, or even put the entire electrical network of a target country out of commission.[4] Nuclear weapons may also produce nuclear electromagnetic pulses.

Make no mistake, these robots can easily bruise you, or break your bones. It's literally up to how they're programmed, how fail-safe and glitch-free they are, and if their sensors can perceive when you're close or vulnerable and can tell them to stop a dangerous maneuver.

Most practical robots are going to be built to handle heavy weight or grip items, and by that nature, they're able to cause harm when things go wrong. 
A fragile robot that can't harm humans will be useless and breakable like a cheap kids toy, or only able to perform very VERY light tasks, like a Roomba sweeper.

snippet.textDisplay:
The RAM crisis WILL end. Be Patient.

For the last few years, making an AI model 10x bigger made it roughly 10x smarter. In late 2025, researchers started noticing that making models bigger wasn't yielding the same "smarter" results anymore. We are hitting a point where throwing more RAM at the problem isn't fixing it.
Eventually, you reach a point where adding 1% more "smartness" requires 1000% more RAM and power.
​If we hit the Soft-Cap: AI progress slows, demand for RAM drops, prices crash. (Gamers Win)
​If we break the Soft-Cap with Efficiency (Mamba/SSMs): AI gets smarter but uses less RAM. Demand drops, prices crash. (Gamers Win)
​If we try to break it with Brute Force: We just keep buying more RAM until the power grid fails. (Gamers Lose)
